reviews.text: It's a fun, surprisingly deep roguelike autobuilder. Lots of strategies to use to break the game (I've discovered a few myself, excited to try a few more out on my next playthrough), it feels really rewarding when your strategy to win comes together and you start annihilating monsters. Game is also very good about politely waiting for you to take your turn if you need to get up and take care of things in real life. At $5 this game is definitely worth a play
the monkey god giveth, the monkey god taketh away

Took down Burny Sanders in one turn, with the help of: * Three piles of water that normally do zero damage but were powered up by game developers * A canister that an anarchist turned into 11 grenades * A small army of civilians-♥♥♥-solders that were recruited from one sodier 10/10 would play again
Mechanically this is similar to Luck be a Landlord. I think that is great, because LbaL has an original feel and its approach to a 'builder' is fresh, I could play many more games in the same vein.
10/10 would totally fight a giant tick with a bunch of overpowered water given +damage by a software developer and some mutant shellfish again.

Great game, lots of potential. Just not a lot of content at the time of me writing this review. Only 2 difficulties (12 bosses vs 13 bosses with more HP), 3 starting layouts, which just means 5 civilians vs 5 zombies vs 5 rats. There are balance issues. Right now, there is no reason to not go humans all the way. You will be cranking out 15k/turn damage easily. The runs are so short, and there are no consistent ways to remove chosen mobs. So you are stuck with what you start to go for, as the synergies are too important to not. I hope this game gets a lot of love, as I can see myself dropped dozens of hours over the months.

中评，基本没有超出幸运房东的东西，甚至讲一个战斗的故事这种套路也有前人走过了，具体来说： - 数值上划分了base/bonus damage、multiplier三者，硬要说肯定是比value-multiplier的二元数值系统能玩出更多花样，对血量和敌人伤害的操作也使得固定轮次有些许的浮动空间 - 完全基于道具的老虎机（没有trinket），但道具之间的交互有点太散了，很多体系都是全靠某几个甚至一个关键道具撑起来的，使得道具选择的决策目的性过于强烈，或者大部分决策对deckbuilding的作用微乎其微，随机性的作用流于表面；由于同样的原因，初始编队对策略的影响大都也不明显 - 每次roll之后主动发动的道具功能本可以是一个不错的差异化方向，但目前来说能发挥这样的道具太少了（IAO、EMP） - remove的功能给的非常稀缺，除了不稳定的各种道具被动只有上面提到的EMP一种稳定的方法，reroll也是简单粗暴的全部一次；虽然本身倒不至于成为问题，但历史经验表明这两者作为通用资源可以提供更多的决策选择 - 由于没有全局成长机制，更高的难度除了有放逐到hell这种机制外与其它难度并无区别，那拼的完全就是敌人的血量曲线和我方的(累计)伤害曲线哪个增长更快了——好吧，我承认几个幸运房东like在这面基本是半斤八两

This game is wonderful. if you've played games like 'Luck be a Landlord', 'Crop Rotation' and even 'Balatro', this game will fit very nicely into your collection. It's addictive and deep and no slouch for difficulty as you must really pay attention to synergy in order to survive. games can be really quick when you're learning but take much longer if you're on a roll. All in all, a gem in the rough and should be much more popular than it is!

It's only a few bucks, buy it. Played this first as a demo before it came to steam, and loved it then even with less content. It is in early access, but honestly it has enough content and value for the asking price on Steam. Game does get updated by devs, it hasn't been abandoned, but don't expect weekly updates. Strategies can get surprisingly deep, and it always feels good to see your plan comes together. Had great fun challenging friends and sharing strats previously and look forward to doing it again now there's more content.

Charming game, but hard to love at its current level of randomness. There are just too many trash choices (who loves "empty cans" or "water"?) and long-shot options ("this thing will be awesome... if you collect 5!") to wade through, and not enough ability to hone a strategy or build synergy. Effectively, the best way to play is to pick a strategy [i]before you start playing,[/i] then carry through and [i]hope it works out.[/i] (and it rarely works out) Abilities to fix or adjust the card pool are super rare, so experimentation in the vein of "let's see if this works!" is often punished. Not an ideal outcome for a roguelike, even a deckbuilder. Worth your money? Sure, it's cheap fun. But is it worth your time? Maybe. It's not worth mine, and it won't be on release unless major changes are made to the way card choices are selected. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

If you enjoy finding combos to break games, this is for you! In the vein of Luck be a Landlord, but with more chaos and far more jokes.

TLDR: Too buggy and mechanically inconsistent to recommend right now. I will switch this if the devs fix this stuff. Bug List: 1. Entering and exiting the tutorial/starter levels removes the unit lock. Meaning you can enter the demon level, quit the game, go back in and no longer be locked to demons. 2. Mutant Juggernaut can trigger early. I think what's happening is that when it has a single unit near it, and you manually trigger that unit, the unit gets removed twice,doubling its damage. But it's not how the wording of the unit describes what should happen. Accidently going over the 25% and losing a run feels bad. 3. Lots of Hellhounds/Dogcatchers tanks the frame rate. 4. Tower of Retribution - Says it's only offered once per militia, I've seen it show up twice in a row. 5. Writer - I don't know if I'm just illiterate, but this guy blows himself up WAY earlier than expected. "Generates a book if fewer than 5 are deployed" 5 what? Books? Units? Writers? And I've never seen him generate 10 books even once. 6. Garbage Collector - Blows itself up even if it doesn't grab 8 units. Again, this could just be wording. If it is, maybe that should just read "Destroys itself after 8 deployments" like every other unit that has this sort of behavior. 7. Internal Affairs Officer - Removes itself after dismissing a single unit instead of 3. 8. Mirror Demon - Text is "Bosses Encountered", but it's actually "Bosses Defeated" I have other thoughts and complaints, but right now, this game is just broken or poorly worded in a stupid number of places, and it makes it incredibly frustrating.

The more you play, the more the game opens up, the more fun you have. The intro helps guide players through the iterative process of learning from your mistakes and finding OP combos. Way more depth and fun than Luck Be a Landlord. This one's a blast.

Is there content here? Yes Have the devs made it fun? No. Learning at the start, you check out plenty of classes and feel the game has some serious depth. And it does! There are plenty of cool things that work with one another but the problem is that the rounds go too high without any sort of modifiers. You end up having to do the same sort of reliable combos over experimentation. This is something that can be easily fixed by adding more unique modifiers throughout the campaign but they struggle to do the bare minimum to even get you there. You unlock new starting teams but those starters don't even remotely matter because the goal you have set is so high. You can't reach it without a reliable infinitely stacking combo. It's a shame because the game is fun if it had some tweaks. The campaign just feels like the same thing over and over and not in the good way. Nothing feels unique. It's just boring. Can't recommend in its current state.
*Do not* add Monkey God to your militia. It *will* show up on the final boss on your last sliver of health and ruin your day.
It was fun until the start of Mission 1, when I had to keep grinding to get that perfect combo going. So I'm calling it quits here.

Sat down to try out the game. Played for three hours. As a fan of Luck Be a Landlord, Endgame of Devil and emergent gameplay, I really dig this game! 18 hours in. Still enjoying the game BUT success IS HIGHLY dependent on RNG with little you can do to mitigate it, at least at 18 hours in. I have played the same battle over dozens of times only to come up short at the last boss. Difficult but enjoyable but I feel that it needs more ways to leverage the RNG and roll-overs for unit stats are sorely needed.
Such a painful game to play. Nothing to balance the game, just has a ton of content and has been abandoned by the creator. Also has a very weird story.

Really wanted to like the game, but some very strange design decisions. Being punished for doing well early forces you into very specific curves of build powers. Huge reliance on luck, which normally would be fine but the runs are very long. This is compounded by the fact that the game lacks basic QOL features like animation skips/options.

It starts fun, then reveals how little it cares about your input. At first glance, this game seems promising. The art's solid, the idea is interesting, and it feels like there's room for creative builds. But once you get past the honeymoon phase, it becomes clear: the whole thing is a dice roll pretending to be a strategy game. Everything relies on luck. There’s almost no player agency after the initial pick, and even that is manipulated. Challenges routinely hand you garbage units (zombies that heal bosses, for example), and the only "solution" is to replay the same scenario over and over until the RNG finally cuts you a break. Worse, the devs have confirmed that some units have intentionally lowered drop rates in certain challenges—meaning even if you figure out what build would work, the game goes out of its way to keep it from you. It’s like they’re daring you to have fun. And if you bring this up? You’ll get the usual canned “this might not be the game for you” response, or a smug “we meant for it to be this way.” It’s clear they’re not interested in feedback unless it’s praise. Honestly, it feels like they paced the game just well enough early on to get people past the Steam refund window before the real frustration kicks in. After that, it’s just grind and pray. If you enjoy watching chaos unfold with basically no control, maybe you’ll have fun here. But if you’re looking for something where your decisions actually matter? This ain’t it.

Once I passed the Prologue it became far more difficult to synergize my build or be able to deal any considerable damage. The only builds I've had consistent success with are those that mark your units for destruction, the irony being if you destroy too much you won't be left with anything to deal damage in the first place.. Chaos and randomness is always fun but when there's too much it leads to frustration and not being able to progress, therefore I think I'm just going to uninstall this. I will say I enjoyed my time with the Prologue missions but after that my enjoyment crashed and burned. I can't say I'd recommend this game.

I got this game not because I thought it was good, but because I appreciated its sense of humour, and the art style is great. Overall it kinda sucks, it's a bit buggy in the very annoying way, the UI is hostile in a few aspects, and there are missions (and their connected achievements and unlockables) that seem to simply not be accessible at all. Oh also there's text from the monsters talking about some big bad called "Ezra" I think it was. You never see him.

I like roguelike deckbuilders. Deckbuilders in general really. So after playing the game for a bit I can say that it's really disappointing. RNG is king here, and unlike games such as Luck be a Landlord, you get pitiful amounts of control over most mechanics. Game mechanics like rerolling/banishing options are either woefully underdeveloped or non-existent. If the game is on sale and you can get it for 1-2 dollars, and you can't find any other deckbuilders that you haven't played already, and you only plan on playing for 1-2 hours at most, then I'd say it's worth buying. But if you play any longer than that you'll realize the game is about as deep as a 1.3oz can of pringles, and it's not even the flavor you like.

Fun little auto-battler-ish. Quite similar to "Luck be a Landlord", but with very different aesthetics. Draft a unit into your pool each round. Units combine in fun and surprising ways. As you learn more about combinations, you'll find interesting strategies.

I like the premise of the game pretty well-- It is effectively Luck be a Landlord, but re-framed to be about a monster militia instead of a slot machine. The thing that eventually put me off, though, is that I just think the difficulty is tuned up too high. The big appeal of a game like this (and in fact one of its advertising points) is finding which units synergize with others to help you rack up massive point combos. But in this one, it feels like the developer tried to prevent as many overpowered strategies from emerging as possible. I could see many units and unit combinations that have the POTENTIAL to become overpowered, but then those units have a hard cap on how many times they can be used before they just disappear. On top of that, there are very limited options for luck manipulation when it comes time to add a new unit to your "deck." You'll be shown a choice of 6, with exactly 1 reroll, and sometimes the reroll shows you some of the same units as your first roll. Sometimes your choices are limited to the "common" rarity pool with none of the higher rarities showing up, and sometimes that's actually beneficial to your build, but other than that you don't have much influence on the choices you're given, and a run just ends due to not being offered anything that helps your build. I wrote this review after playing over a dozen unsuccessful runs in a row, and in a game where luck is such a pivotal factor, I'd prefer to play something that's more generous to the player. The game could benefit from more variety, like if some of the enemies had differences beyond their name and appearance, or again if there were more ways to manipulate your luck or units offered. The UI could also use some work. For example, sometimes a unit's description says that it transforms into a different unit or creates another unit; Could really use a pop-up describing what those other units are. I may give it another chance one day, but as of now I think I hit the tipping point from fun to frustration.
First Impressions: A Recruitment Roguelite Autobattler which allows for seemingly endless combinations - from Civilians, to Bunnies and Dragons. Very addicting to play, but I worry for its longevity.
